links.citation: Wikipedia/Neu!: formed in 1971 in Düsseldorf as an offshoot of an early Kraftwerk lineup -- Michael Rother and Klaus Dinger both played in Kraftwerk 1970-71 before splitting off.

Record Collector wrote that Nick Drake was fascinated with Bert Jansch's guitar playing; Totally Guitar dates his interest to 1965, describing him as influenced by the folk movement and artists including Jansch, Bob Dylan and Jackson C. Frank; Acoustic Guitar documents his home recordings including Jansch's "Strolling Down the Highway."
Acoustic Guitar documents Nick Drake's home recordings as including Bob Dylan's "Tomorrow Is a Long Time."
Wikipedia Legacy section; no reproduced quote found, flagged weaker-tier.

FarOut Magazine ("The surprising early influences on the music of Silver Apples") and Wikipedia/Silver Apples list Stereolab among influenced artists; Stereolab's Tim Gane separately cited Silver Apples as a favorite record in a 1993 interview.

Billboard's account of the Savage/Duff liner-note essays for Wire's reissues describes what the band was listening to at the time, and Rolling Stone has written about Berlin-era David Bowie's heavy influence on Wire's third album, 154.

Ilana Kaplan, SPIN (11 Mar 2015), "SXSW Lone Stars: Alvvays on Archie's Identity and Scot-Pop," and Rebecca Schiller, Diffuser.fm (21 Nov 2014) both report Pavement among Molly Rankin's named influences. Reported as a name on her own list rather than a claim she elaborates on, hence the lower confidence.

The Independent described James Murphy as an avid student of the Birthday Party, alongside Can, the Velvet Underground and what it called "weird punk rock."
The same Independent profile named the Velvet Underground among the artists James Murphy studied closely, alongside the Birthday Party and Can.

Codeine predate and are widely cited as a formative reference point for the slowcore sound Low worked in; the same lineage claim recurs independently in Duster's and American Football's own accounts of what they were listening to.
Wikipedia/Suicide: Alan Vega directly cited the Velvet Underground, Iggy Pop, ? and the Mysterians, and Silver Apples as influences.
FarOut Magazine ("Exploring the early influences of Suicide founder Martin Rev"): Vega "was blown away when he saw The Stooges in 1969, going home to play 'I Wanna Be Your Dog' on repeat."

A 1996 copy of Boards of Canada's Twoism reached Sean Booth, who championed the duo to Skam Records; Booth supplied a numbers-station recording for "Gyroscope," and Boards of Canada recorded an unreleased cover of Autechre's "Cichli."
The same rare Pitchfork interview: the duo say they are big fans of the Cocteau Twins and My Bloody Valentine.
